prompt.en: Arjun says: "A tree trunk gets thicker over the years because its old cells slowly stretch wider." What is wrong with Arjun's idea? Explain how a trunk really gets thicker.

level1.en: When a cell stretches, does the number of cells in the trunk change?

clue.en: A cell can stretch only a little, and stretching does not make any new cells.

level2Template.en: Stretching cannot make a trunk much thicker, because stretching does not add any new ___.

label.en: The lateral meristem adds new cells

level1.en: Which tissue in the stem keeps making new cells for girth, and where is it?

clue.en: A ring of dividing cells in the stem adds new cells on its inside and its outside.

level2Template.en: A ring of dividing cells in the stem, called the ___, adds new cells and makes the trunk thicker.

text.en: A cell can stretch only a little, and stretching adds no new cells.
The lateral meristem, a ring of dividing cells in the stem, adds new cells inside and outside, so the trunk gets thicker.
